cards.title: Bringing Fantasy Characters to Life: Samsung Spatial Signage Transforms Tokyo Game Show 2026
cards.title_cn: 将奇幻角色带入生活：三星空间标牌改变 2026 年东京游戏展
cards.summary: 【Samsung】At Tokyo Game Show (TGS) 2026, held from September 17 to 20 at Makuhari Messe in Chiba, Japan, Samsung Electronics and NC demonstrated the future of fan engagement by bringing the characters of Astrae…
fulltext: Samsung Newsroom
on September 23, 2026

At Tokyo Game Show (TGS) 2026, held from September 17 to 20 at Makuhari Messe in Chiba, Japan, Samsung Electronics and NC demonstrated the future of fan engagement by bringing the characters of Astrae Oratio — the upcoming urban fantasy RPG — into the physical world through glasses-free 3D Spatial Signage.
The installation transformed a conventional booth into an immersive experience where visitors encountered lifelike characters at scale, blurring the line between digital worlds and physical spaces.
For game publishers and IP owners, the challenge lies in translating digital characters into physical environments.

At the entrance to the booth of NC, a global game developer and publishing company, an 85-inch Spatial Signage display was integrated into an elevator-themed installation and introduced Astrae Oratio characters at near life-size scale. Featuring Samsung’s patented 3D Plate technology, Spatial Signage created a vivid sense of depth without requiring viewers to wear 3D glasses, bringing the game’s characters and its magical world into the physical space.

“We wanted visitors to come face-to-face with the characters at life-size scale and feel immersed in the game’s world from the moment they entered the booth,” said Yongsoo Lee, Head of Astrae Oratio Business Division at NC. “For games in the subculture genre, the liveliness and realism of the characters are especially important. We believed that Samsung Spatial Signage would make this possible.”
Visitors responded immediately to the display’s scale, movement, and sense of depth.

Content creator Kawaii CoCo noted, “The character felt interactive because she was moving around, which made her feel a little more human-like. That really caught my attention.” She added that the display’s social media presence was undeniable. “It’s much more prominent and looks much better on social media, so I wanted to capture some footage and show my audience this really cool display.”

Despite its slim 52mm profile,1 Spatial Signage is designed to create the visual impression of depth, making it appear as though the space extends behind the screen. This immersive effect creates a powerful impression when viewers first encounter a game and its characters in public settings.

Booth visitor Daniel Acero said, “Having this as the first impression of the game in public is really helpful for shaping public perception of the game. It also conveys the personalities of the characters.” He added, “I didn’t realize it was a display screen. I thought it was a transparent screen with an actual space behind it. It really created a strong sense of depth.”

Beyond the entrance, compact 32-inch Spatial Signage displays, with an even slimmer profile of 49.4mm, were placed in waiting areas and along the visitor route, extending the character experience throughout the booth. The smaller form factor enabled flexible installation in space-constrained areas while helping visitors remain engaged with the game’s characters and its world as they waited.

Visitor Tomas Portier said, “Even if the queue was kind of long, Spatial Signage helped the time pass more quickly while helping me get to know the characters a little better. It’s more lively than a still image or a conventional screen.”

For retailers and venue operators, visual impact needs to work within the realities of physical space. Spatial Signage’s slim profile, combined with glasses-free 3D presentation, enabled NC to make strategic use of limited space.

“Designing the visitor flow was quite challenging, but since Spatial Signage is very slim, it was really easy to install and make effective use of the space,” Yongsoo Lee explained. “That also gave us room to store merchandise for visitors.”

At the booth entrance, NC used the installation as both a visual focal point and a functional part of the layout. While the display captured visitors’ attention, the area behind it provided concealed storage for merchandise.
Visitor David Yousefi observed, “When you present it like this in a box, I thought it was much larger.” He added, “But it’s pretty cool that you can put it all into such a limited space.”
This flexibility could help character IP owners, retailers, and venue operators bring content into a wider range of physical environments.

Miguel Moren, a gaming industry professional and TGS 2026 exhibitor, said, “Having animated video game characters in a real-life space creates a really nice blend of the imaginary world and the real world.”
Visitors expressed enthusiasm about potential applications beyond gaming events.

Rio Matsushita suggested, “I think having your favorite character move right in front of you is a really great experience. Even while waiting, I could clearly see the three-dimensional visuals. I think it would be a lot of fun if we could see something like that in places like Akihabara too.”

Nicolas Felix also saw other opportunities for Spatial Signage. “I think it could be used for commercial branding in shops, for example, to showcase clothes on people,” he said. Yousefi also pointed to additional applications in other public-facing environments. “I could also see it being successful in theme parks or other events where you want to showcase something.”

The Tokyo Game Show installation is one of several commercial deployments of Samsung Spatial Signage across entertainment, retail, and event environments. At Everland Safari World in Korea, it was integrated into the attraction’s waiting queue, extending the safari experience into areas traditionally reserved for crowd management. The Governors Ball Music Festival in the United States showcased merchandise on an 85-inch display, integrating commerce into the live-event experience.

These installations demonstrate how Spatial Signage brings digital content to physical space through a combination of visual impact, spatial efficiency, and visitor engagement. With a range of display sizes and a form factor designed to integrate seamlessly into existing environments, the technology enables storytelling opportunities in spaces where conventional displays have been limited.

cards.summary_cn: 【Samsung】在 9 月 17 日至 20 日在日本千叶幕张展览馆举行的 2026 年东京游戏展 (TGS) 上，三星电子和 NC 通过带来 Astrae 角色展示了粉丝参与度的未来……
fulltext_cn: 三星新闻中心
在 9 月 17 日至 20 日在日本千叶幕张展览馆举行的 2026 年东京游戏展 (TGS) 上，三星电子和 NC 通过裸眼 3D 空间标牌将即将推出的都市奇幻角色扮演游戏 Astrae Oratio 的角色带入现实世界，展示了粉丝参与的未来。
该装置将传统的展位转变为一种身临其境的体验，参观者可以大规模地遇到栩栩如生的角色，模糊了数字世界和物理空间之间的界限。
对于游戏发行商和 IP 所有者来说，挑战在于将数字角色转化为物理环境。
在全球游戏开发商和发行公司NC的展位入口处，85英寸的空间标牌显示屏被集成到以电梯为主题的装置中，并以接近真人大小的比例介绍了Astrae Oratio角色。 Spatial Signage 采用三星专利 3D Plate 技术，无需观众佩戴 3D 眼镜即可营造生动的深度感，将游戏角色及其魔法世界带入物理空间。
NC Astrae Oratio 业务部主管 Yongsoo Lee 表示：“我们希望参观者能够与真人大小的角色面对面，并从进入展位的那一刻起就感受到沉浸在游戏世界中。” “对于亚文化类型的游戏来说，角色的生动性和真实感尤其重要。我们相信三星空间标牌将使这一切成为可能。”
参观者立即对展示的规模、动感和深度感做出了反应。
内容创作者 Kawaii CoCo 指出：“这个角色感觉互动，因为她在四处走动，这让她感觉更像人类。这确实引起了我的注意。”她补充说，该显示器在社交媒体上的存在是不可否认的。 “它在社交媒体上更加突出，看起来也更好，所以我想捕捉一些镜头并向观众展示这个非常酷的展示。”
尽管外形纤薄，只有 52 毫米，1 空间标牌的设计目的是营造深度的视觉印象，使其看起来好像空间延伸到屏幕后面。当观众第一次在公共环境中遇到游戏及其角色时，这种身临其境的效果会给人留下深刻的印象。
展位参观者 Daniel Acero 表示：“将其作为公众对游戏的第一印象，对于塑造公众对游戏的认知确实很有帮助。它还传达了角色的个性。”他补充道，“我没有意识到这是一个显示屏。我以为这是一个透明的屏幕，后面有一个实际的空间。它确实创造了很强的深度感。”
除了入口之外，等候区和访客路线沿线还放置了紧凑型 32 英寸空间标牌显示屏，其外形更为纤薄，仅为 49.4 毫米，从而扩展了整个展位的角色体验。较小的外形尺寸可以在空间有限的区域进行灵活的安装，同时帮助游客在等待时保持与游戏角色和世界的互动。
参观者托马斯·波蒂尔 (Tomas Portier) 表示：“即使队列有点长，空间标牌也让时间过得更快，同时帮助我更好地了解角色。它比静止图像或传统屏幕更生动。”
对于零售商和场馆运营商来说，视觉效果需要在物理空间的现实中发挥作用。 Spatial Signage 的纤薄外形与裸眼 3D 演示相结合，使 NC 能够战略性地利用有限的空间。
“设计访客流程相当具有挑战性，但由于空间标牌非常纤薄，因此安装和有效利用空间非常容易，”Yongsoo Lee 解释道。 “这也为我们提供了为游客储存商品的空间。”
在展位入口处，NC 使用该装置作为布局的视觉焦点和功能部分。虽然展示吸引了参观者的注意力，但其后面的区域提供了隐藏的商品存储空间。
参观者 David Yousefi 观察到，“当你像这样把它装在盒子里时，我觉得它要大得多。”他补充道，“但是你可以将所有东西都放入如此有限的空间中，这真是太酷了。”
这种灵活性可以帮助角色 IP 所有者、零售商和场馆运营商将内容带入更广泛的物理环境中。
游戏行业专业人士兼 TGS 2026 参展商 Miguel Moren 表示：“在现实生活空间中加入动画视频游戏角色，创造了想象世界与现实世界的完美融合。”
参观者对游戏活动之外的潜在应用表示了热情。
松下里奥表示：“我认为让你最喜欢的角色在你面前移动是一种非常好的体验。即使在等待的时候，我也可以清楚地看到三维视觉效果。我认为如果我们也能在秋叶原这样的地方看到类似的东西，那会很有趣。”
尼古拉斯·菲利克斯 (Nicolas Felix) 还看到了空间标牌的其他机会。 “我认为它可以用于商店的商业品牌推广，例如，向人们展示衣服，”他说。 Yousefi 还指出了其他面向公众的环境中的其他应用程序。 “我还可以看到它在主题公园或其他想要展示某些东西的活动中取得成功。”
东京游戏展的安装是三星空间标牌在娱乐、零售和活动环境中的多项商业部署之一。在韩国的爱宝乐园野生动物世界，它被整合到景点的等候队列中，将野生动物体验扩展到传统上用于人群管理的区域。美国州长舞会音乐节在 85 英寸显示屏上展示商品，将商业融入现场活动体验。
这些装置展示了空间标牌如何通过视觉冲击力、空间效率和访客参与的结合将数字内容带入物理空间。该技术具有多种显示器尺寸和旨在无缝集成到现有环境的外形尺寸，可以在传统显示器受到限制的空间中提供讲故事的机会。

cards.title: At AI Day Singapore, NVIDIA and Partners Showcase AI Advancements Across Southeast Asia
cards.title_cn: 在新加坡 AI Day 上，NVIDIA 及其合作伙伴展示了整个东南亚的 AI 进步
cards.summary: 【NVIDIA】NVIDIA AI Day Singapore , which takes place Sept. 22-23 at the Raffles City Convention Centre, is offering attendees opportunities to explore the hands-on training, expert-led sessions and advanced to…
fulltext: Share This Article

NVIDIA AI Day Singapore, which takes place Sept. 22-23 at the Raffles City Convention Centre, is offering attendees opportunities to explore the hands-on training, expert-led sessions and advanced tools to accelerate their work in AI and high-performance computing.
At the event, NVIDIA and its partners are showcasing breakthrough AI advancements across the Southeast Asia region at large.

AI is becoming a matter of national strategy, with governments looking to move from pilots to production and deliver impact at scale, while building trusted AI capabilities that reflect local languages, cultures, priorities and economic needs.

NVIDIA is working to enable all nations to be AI nations — providing the technology, infrastructure, ecosystem and expertise needed to make this possible. To accelerate this transition across Southeast Asia, NVIDIA is helping nations move AI from experimentation to production-scale deployment through open models, developer tools and a broad partner ecosystem.
Together, NVIDIA and its partners are focusing on four key areas:

Singapore’s HTX (Home Team Science and Technology Agency) is embarking on research using the NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super and Nemotron 3 Nano Omni models to advance AI for public safety. Nemotron Super has the potential to support the agency’s complex reasoning and agentic workflows, while Omni’s unified vision, audio and language capabilities could help HTX develop multimodal applications grounded in real-world operational data. Together, the models could strengthen HTX’s ability to deploy secure, locally controlled AI across Singapore’s Home Team.

NCS is advancing agentic AI adoption across enterprises and the public sector, using Nemotron models and the NVIDIA Blueprint for video search and summarization (VSS), while advancing physical AI for practical humanoid robotics applications, to address security, responsiveness and data governance requirements. ST Engineering is using NVIDIA NeMo tools and NVIDIA cuOpt software to develop its AI Studio platform and deploy agentic AI solutions across its businesses such as Marine MRO.

Beyond Singapore, similar work is already underway across the region. Malaysia’s YTL AI Labs is fine-tuning Nemotron models for enterprise and citizen services, while Viettel AI is doing the same for Vietnamese-language applications.

In Thailand, the Big Data Institute and iApp Technology, as members of the ThaiLLM Collaboration, are exploring Nemotron as a foundation model. With an initial focus on legal applications, iApp Technology is adapting Nemotron 3 Nano by fine-tuning OpenThai 2.0 Legal with Thai-language legal data using the NVIDIA NeMo framework.
The model is released as open source for the Thai developer community and serves as the engine for Thanoy, the company’s legal-assistant chatbot, which already serves approximately 43,000 users.
In Brunei, Antrique built an AI innovation platform to help boost productivity across the nation’s food sector.

Across the region, NVIDIA Cosmos open world models and the NVIDIA VSS Blueprint are advancing smart city solution development. Malaysia’s ITMAX uses Cosmos with VSS to improve city traffic operations, while Thailand’s AS-TECH applies the same stack to improve passenger flow in airports.
Learn more about NVIDIA Nemotron and Cosmos models and read about NVIDIA’s participation in the Open Secure AI Alliance.

Leading enterprises, technology providers and research organizations across Southeast Asia are building region-specialized AI models and applications with NVIDIA Nemotron open models, datasets and libraries — accelerating the development of AI tailored to the region’s languages, industries and communities.

NVIDIA Nemotron provides a foundation for regional AI ecosystems, letting organizations customize, control and own models that address their specific requirements. Nemotron also offers persona datasets that provide locally relevant synthetic data reflecting the region’s populations, languages and workforces.
Across the region, partners are building applications spanning public services, services and healthcare.

Enterprises in Singapore are adopting NVIDIA Nemotron for various use cases. AI Singapore is expanding its SEA-LION model family to include the NVIDIA Nemotron open models and NVIDIA NeMo tools. SEA-LION is an open model family designed for Southeast Asian languages and cultures.

Hummingbird Bioscience, together with LynxKite, is building an explainable Toxicity Knowledge Graph powered by Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Retriever with in silico simulations. The collaboration aims to integrate complex public and proprietary data across diverse third-party file formats, creating a comprehensive, unified foundation for robust analysis and reasoning that helps de-risk and accelerate drug discovery and development.

Bitdeer AI co-hosted the Open Models AI Codefest with NVIDIA, providing the GPU cloud infrastructure that enabled developers across the region to use NVIDIA Nemotron open models, datasets and training recipes to accelerate localized applications across critical sectors, including healthcare.

In Vietnam, Viettel AI has been extensively fine-tuning Nemotron 3 Super for the Vietnamese language and agentic applications. The model achieved the highest ranking on both the VMLU benchmark and the company’s in-house product benchmark, and it’s set to be adopted in Legal AI — an agent harness that will serve both internal Viettel Group employees and external customers.

Also in Vietnam, FPT Smart Cloud codeveloped Nemotron-Personas-Vietnam, an open dataset grounded in Vietnamese demographic and cultural data, and is enabling local developers to post-train and evaluate localized AI models.
Get started building with NVIDIA Nemotron using skills and playbooks that help partners customize Nemotron open models for their languages and domains.
Stay up to date on agentic AI, NVIDIA Nemotron and more by subscribing to NVIDIA news, joining the community and following NVIDIA AI on LinkedIn, Instagram, X and Facebook.
Explore self-paced video tutorials and livestreams.

Sea Limited, a global technology company founded in Singapore, is the first enterprise in the ASEAN region to adopt the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, further strengthening the company’s AI capabilities to better serve and create meaningful economic opportunities for millions of consumers and small businesses across Southeast Asia.

Serving hundreds of millions of users through its Garena, Monee and Shopee platforms, Sea has already deployed AI across its businesses to make its services more useful and accessible. Now, with NVIDIA Vera Rubin, Sea will build on these efforts, developing and deploying AI models and intelligent agents at greater scale to serve the evolving needs of its communities.

On Shopee, AI is already helping sellers reduce the time and effort required to create informative product listings, improve product discovery and deepen customer engagement, while enabling better-informed business decisions. These capabilities enable small- and medium-sized enterprises in Southeast Asia, many of which operate with limited resources, to scale their businesses using enterprise-grade AI technologies previously accessible only to large corporations.

Across Monee, the digital financial services division of Sea, AI is being applied in areas such as fraud detection and credit risk assessment, supporting Monee’s ability to deliver simple, accessible and inclusive digital financial services. For small businesses and consumers underserved by traditional financial services, these capabilities can expansively broaden access to financial tools.

At Garena, Sea’s digital entertainment and video game arm, AI is used to enhance gaming experiences supporting the company’s efforts to create engaging, inclusive and safe online spaces that bring players together.

NVIDIA Vera Rubin will provide the advanced computing infrastructure to build on this foundation — enabling Sea to accelerate innovation, scale AI applications more broadly and deepen its impact for the communities it serves.
Learn more about NVIDIA Vera Rubin.

fulltext_cn: 分享这篇文章
新加坡 NVIDIA 人工智能日将于 9 月 22 日至 23 日在莱佛士城会议中心举行，为与会者提供探索实践培训、专家主导的课程和先进工具的机会，以加速他们在人工智能和高性能计算方面的工作。
在此次活动中，NVIDIA 及其合作伙伴展示了整个东南亚地区突破性的人工智能进步。
人工智能正在成为国家战略问题，各国政府希望从试点转向生产并产生大规模影响，同时建立反映当地语言、文化、优先事项和经济需求的可信人工智能能力。
NVIDIA 致力于让所有国家成为人工智能国家，提供实现这一目标所需的技术、基础设施、生态系统和专业知识。为了加速整个东南亚的这一转变，NVIDIA 正在通过开放模型、开发者工具和广泛的合作伙伴生态系统，帮助各国将人工智能从实验阶段转向生产规模部署。
NVIDIA 及其合作伙伴共同关注四个关键领域：

新加坡 HTX（Home Team Science and Technology Agency）正在着手使用 NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Super 和 Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 模型进行研究，以推进人工智能促进公共安全。 Nemotron Super 有潜力支持该机构的复杂推理和代理工作流程，而 Omni 的统一视觉、音频和语言功能可以帮助 HTX 开发基于实际操作数据的多模式应用程序。这些模型共同可以增强 HTX 在新加坡主队部署安全、本地控制的人工智能的能力。

NCS 正在推动代理 AI 在企业和公共部门的采用，使用 Nemotron 模型和 NVIDIA 蓝图进行视频搜索和摘要 (VSS)，同时推进实际人形机器人应用的物理 AI，以满足安全性、响应能力和数据治理要求。 ST Engineering 正在使用 NVIDIA NeMo 工具和 NVIDIA cuOpt 软件来开发其 AI Studio 平台，并在其业务（例如船舶 MRO）中部署代理 AI 解决方案。
除了新加坡之外，整个地区也已经开展了类似的工作。马来西亚的 YTL AI 实验室正在针对企业和公民服务微调 Nemotron 模型，而 Viettel AI 也在为越南语应用程序做同样的事情。
在泰国，大数据研究所和 iApp Technology 作为 ThaiLLM Collaboration 的成员，正在探索 Nemotron 作为基础模型。 iApp Technology 最初专注于法律应用，目前正在使用 NVIDIA NeMo 框架对 OpenThai 2.0 Legal 与泰语法律数据进行微调，以适应 Nemotron 3 Nano。
该模型作为泰国开发者社区的开源版本发布，并作为该公司法律助理聊天机器人 Thanoy 的引擎，该机器人已经为大约 43,000 名用户提供服务。
在文莱，Antrique 建立了一个人工智能创新平台，以帮助提高该国食品行业的生产力。
在整个地区，NVIDIA Cosmos 开放世界模型和 NVIDIA VSS 蓝图正在推动智慧城市解决方案的开发。马来西亚的 ITMAX 使用 Cosmos 和 VSS 来改善城市交通运营，而泰国的 AS-TECH 应用相同的堆栈来改善机场的客流。
了解有关 NVIDIA Nemotron 和 Cosmos 模型的更多信息，并了解 NVIDIA 参与开放安全 AI 联盟的信息。
东南亚各地的领先企业、技术提供商和研究组织正在利用 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型、数据集和库构建区域专用的 AI 模型和应用程序，从而加速针对该地区语言、行业和社区的 AI 开发。
NVIDIA Nemotron 为区域人工智能生态系统奠定了基础，让组织可以定制、控制和拥有满足其特定需求的模型。 Nemotron 还提供角色数据集，提供反映该地区人口、语言和劳动力的本地相关综合数据。
在整个地区，合作伙伴正在构建涵盖公共服务、服务和医疗保健的应用程序。
新加坡的企业正在针对各种用例采用 NVIDIA Nemotron。 AI Singapore 正在扩展其 SEA-LION 模型系列，以纳入 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型和 NVIDIA NeMo 工具。 SEA-LION 是一个专为东南亚语言和文化设计的开放模型系列。
Hummingbird Bioscience 与 LynxKite 一起，正在通过计算机模拟构建由 Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 和 NeMo Retriever 提供支持的可解释的毒性知识图。此次合作旨在整合不同第三方文件格式的复杂公共和专有数据，为稳健的分析和推理创建全面、统一的基础，有助于降低风险并加速药物发现和开发。
Bitdeer AI 与 NVIDIA 共同主办了 Open Models AI Codefest，提供 GPU 云基础设施，使该地区的开发人员能够使用 NVIDIA Nemotron 开放模型、数据集和训练方法来加速医疗保健等关键领域的本地化应用。
在越南，Viettel AI 已针对越南语和代理应用程序对 Nemotron 3 Super 进行了广泛的微调。该模型在 VMLU 基准和公司内部产品基准上均取得了最高排名，并将在 Legal AI 中采用，这是一种为 Viettel 集团内部员工和外部客户提供服务的代理工具。
同样在越南，FPT Smart Cloud 共同开发了 Nemotron-Personas-Vietnam，这是一个基于越南人口和文化数据的开放数据集，使本地开发人员能够对本地化人工智能模型进行后期训练和评估。
开始使用 NVIDIA Nemotron 进行构建，使用技能和手册帮助合作伙伴为其语言和领域定制 Nemotron 开放模型。
通过订阅 NVIDIA 新闻、加入社区以及在 LinkedIn、Instagram、X 和 Facebook 上关注 NVIDIA AI，了解 Agentic AI、NVIDIA Nemotron 等的最新动态。
探索自定进度的视频教程和直播。
Sea Limited 是一家成立于新加坡的全球科技公司，是东盟地区第一家采用 NVIDIA Vera Rubin 平台的企业，进一步增强该公司的 AI 能力，以更好地服务东南亚数百万消费者和小型企业并创造有意义的经济机会。
Sea 通过其 Garena、Monee 和 Shopee 平台为数亿用户提供服务，并已在其业务中部署人工智能，以使其服务更加有用和易于访问。现在，借助 NVIDIA Vera Rubin，Sea 将在这些努力的基础上更进一步，更大规模地开发和部署 AI 模型和智能代理，以满足社区不断变化的需求。
在 Shopee 上，人工智能已经帮助卖家减少创建信息丰富的产品列表、改善产品发现和加深客户参与所需的时间和精力，同时实现更明智的业务决策。这些功能使东南亚的中小企业（其中许多企业的运营资源有限）能够使用以前只有大公司才能使用的企业级人工智能技术来扩展业务。
在 Sea 的数字金融服务部门 Monee 中，人工智能正在应用于欺诈检测和信用风险评估等领域，支持 Monee 提供简单、可访问和包容性数字金融服务的能力。对于传统金融服务不足的小企业和消费者来说，这些功能可以广泛扩大金融工具的使用范围。
在 Sea 的数字娱乐和视频游戏部门 Garena，人工智能用于增强游戏体验，支持该公司努力创建引人入胜、包容且安全的在线空间，将玩家聚集在一起。
NVIDIA Vera Rubin 将在此基础上提供先进的计算基础设施，使 Sea 能够加速创新、更广泛地扩展 AI 应用并加深对其所服务社区的影响。

cards.title: Here Wallpaper：把喜欢的地图做成壁纸
cards.title_cn: 这里壁纸：把喜欢的地图进口壁纸
cards.summary: 家附近的街道、旅行时喜欢上的一座城市、或者喜欢的海岸线和岛屿，都可以拿来做壁纸。 查看全文
fulltext: Matrix 首页推荐
Matrix 是少数派的写作社区，我们主张分享真实的产品体验，有实用价值的经验与思考。我们会不定期挑选 Matrix 最优质的文章，展示来自用户的最真实的体验和观点。
文章代表作者个人观点，少数派仅对标题和排版略作修改。
家附近的街道、旅行时喜欢上的一座城市、或者喜欢的海岸线和岛屿，都可以拿来做壁纸。放大看，道路交错铺满画面；拉远一些，河流和海岸线就成了主角；再换一套主题配色，同一个地方也能有不同的感觉。
我做的 Here Wallpaper，就是一个用地图制作壁纸的 App。它支持 iPhone、iPad 和 Mac，选好地点，调整比例尺、主题和字体，就能生成漂亮的壁纸，可以把你喜欢的地方放到屏幕上。
打开编辑器可以搜索地点，也可以从当前位置开始。如果你喜欢看街道路线交错，就把地图放大；想看一座城市的轮廓，就把范围拉远。
主题决定地图的配色，图层决定画面里保留多少细节。道路、建筑、水域、公园、铁路和机场等都可以按需显示。你可以保留密集的街道纹理，也可以减少图层，让河流或海岸线更突出。
如果一时想不到选哪里，可以试试「随机地点」。Here Wallpaper 会从内置的精选城市和地标中选择一个地点作为地图中心，给你一个细节调整的起点。
不过因为 Apple 地图 API 限制，国行系统似乎只能搜到国内地点，海外系统没这个限制。
相比手机端，Mac 端可以直接在系统壁纸与桌面图标之间插入一个图层，把地图显示在桌面组件和图标之下（在 Windows 用过壁纸引擎的应该知道什么意思）。打开 Here Wallpaper，地图就会显示在桌面上。
你可以选择在哪个显示器上显示地图，让主题跟随系统明暗外观，也可以开启唤醒设备后自动轮换随机地点。如果在探索应用的过程中遇到想保存的画面，Mac 端也支持导出无损 PNG。
iPhone 和 iPad 上虽然因为 Apple 系统限制无法直接更换壁纸，但你可以把调整好的壁纸加入收藏夹，然后通过快捷指令读取图片并设为系统墙纸。配合个人自动化，还能按时间或其他条件更换。
比如你可以先收藏几张喜欢的地图壁纸，再设置每天早上随机换一张。自动化使用的是提前收藏好的图片，地点、配色和构图都由你事先选好。
如果习惯手动更换，也可以直接将壁纸导出到相册，再设为墙纸。
同一个地方，换一套配色壁纸的感觉就会变。Here Wallpaper 内置了多种地图主题，可以在选好地点后逐一试试，找到适合自己屏幕的那一套。
如果你想自己配色，应用还提供了一个易于上手的自定义主题编辑器。你可以按自己的喜好调整地图配色，让熟悉的街道有一个自己喜欢的样子。地点和构图不变，也能做出不同风格的壁纸。
或者你也可以导出内置主题模版，让 AI 帮忙配色，然后再导入应用中进行设置。
Here Wallpaper 的大部分地图主题配色参考了开源项目 Terraink，早期实现参考了其在 2026 年 4 月 3 日之前以 MIT 许可证发布的源代码。相关项目链接和版权说明已放在 App 的致谢页面中。
Here Wallpaper 支持 iOS26+、iPadOS26+ 和 macOS26+。你可以先从自己住过的一条街开始做几张壁纸，或者直接随机定位到一些我收录的知名景点，看看设置为壁纸的效果。欢迎试用之后提交反馈和建议。

fulltext: IT之家 9 月 23 日消息，华为智能门锁 2 Pro 悦享版今日 10:08 开启预售，到手价 2499 元，部分地区国补后 2124.15 元。
该门锁采用一体化压铸工艺制造，内部配置全自动降噪锁体及 C 级直插式锁芯。产品前面板集成了深感摄像头与 161° 广角智能猫眼，还提供了应急小红键。
IT之家获悉，该门锁设备应用 AI 3D 人脸识别 3.0 及 3D ToF 技术，可捕捉 307,200 个深度信息点，解锁耗时约为 0.8s。其识别范围覆盖 1.2m 至 2.0m 身高以及 0 至 30° 侧脸，配合活体检测及动态学习算法，可识别并拦截照片、视频或 3D 头模干扰。
同时，门锁支持 AI 人形监测及异常抓拍功能，访客按铃后的画面可跨屏推送至手机、智慧屏或中控屏，并支持画中画显示及可视对讲远程解锁。系统同时支持语音留言提醒及出门天气播报功能。
该门锁配备 10000mAh 锂电池，可提供 4 至 6 个月的续航，切换至 4 节 5 号干电池时可维持 7 个月的基础解锁续航。在电量耗尽且关机的状态下，用户按压应急小红键即可启用内部备用供电，通过指纹或密码完成解锁。

cards.title: OpenAI wants to consult elite mathematicians about how to not fumble again
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 希望向精英数学家咨询如何不再失手
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】After turning a string of spectacular mathematical results into a reputational crisis, OpenAI is consulting human mathematicians to help it figure out a less disastrous path forward. On Monday, the co…
fulltext: ﻿‘The group will advise on the review and communication of emerging results.’
After turning a string of spectacular mathematical results into a reputational crisis, OpenAI is consulting human mathematicians to help it figure out a less disastrous path forward.

On Monday, the company announced a new independent panel of mathematicians tasked with advising it and other AI companies on their interactions with mathematical research and the wider mathematics community, including how new results are presented and released. Its abrupt arrival caught many mathematicians by surprise. Researchers told The Verge the group is a good first step, but many said they were left with basic questions about what it will actually do, how much influence it will have, and whether OpenAI will actually listen to it, as well as concerns over whether such a small group of prominent researchers can represent the wider mathematical community.

The nine-member group is stacked with who researchers described to The Verge as celebrities in the field, drawn from institutions including Stanford, Harvard, Oxford, and Cambridge, with multiple Fields Medals and MacArthur “genius grants” among them. It will be hosted by Princeton, New Jersey’s Institute for Advanced Study (IAS), one of the world’s most revered centers of mathematical research and the former intellectual home of figures including Albert Einstein, John von Neumann, and J. Robert Oppenheimer.
“The other fundamental fact is that our overarching aim is to represent as well as we possibly can the interests of the mathematical community.”

OpenAI said the group, called the Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI), will operate independently, with the freedom to offer advice the company has not requested, publicly comment on its impact on mathematics, and make its advice public, though it did not provide details on what this may entail. It appears that the group will be granted early access to OpenAI’s research in order to fulfill its task. Members will not be paid by OpenAI and the group can change its membership as it sees fit, OpenAI said. “Its value depends on its members being able to exercise their own judgement and challenge ours,” the company said. “The group will advise on the review and communication of emerging results: they will help OpenAI assess their significance, advise on how to coordinate their dissemination, and advise on academic and professional standards of mathematical research. It will also advise on how our tools can support mathematical research and learning.”

For all the emphasis on independence, it remains unclear how much influence the group will actually have or why it was formed in the first place. Simon Machado, a researcher at ETH Zurich in Switzerland, said the whole thing seemed “shrouded in mystery” and he questioned how the nine members were selected. The group’s bare-bones website says it “came together after OpenAI approached some of its members about establishing an external advisory board,” but that, following discussions with the company, the mathematicians decided to launch an independent group instead and invite others to join. It’s not clear which members were initially approached by OpenAI or how the remaining members were selected.

In a blog post published Tuesday, advisory group member Martin Hairer elaborated on the group’s origins and the thinking behind it, responding to what he called a “torrent of misinformation” surrounding its formation. “It is obvious that AI has already had a profound impact on mathematical research and raises numerous questions of correct attribution of ideas, priority, human understanding of ideas, etc.,” he wrote, adding that there is no sense in the community “taking a hard ‘ostrich’ approach of simply ignoring the AI labs and refusing to talk to them on principle.”

While acknowledging that the group was formed in response to an approach from OpenAI, Hairer stressed that not all of its members had been contacted by the company and that the resulting organization is “genuinely independent of OpenAI and any other of the so-called ‘frontier’ AI labs.” Beyond “obvious confidentiality requirements,” he said members have not signed any restrictive agreements governing what they can say publicly, adding that they receive no financial compensation and are relying on the IAS for technical support.

“The other fundamental fact is that our overarching aim is to represent as well as we possibly can the interests of the mathematical community,” wrote Hairer, a professor of mathematics at Imperial College London and the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL). While noting that the group is hardly a representative sample of the community, he said he is “absolutely certain that all nine of us take this extremely seriously and are acting in good faith.”

However the members were selected, the group currently comprises an elite cadre of academic mathematicians. The small size raises further questions about whether the group has the breadth of expertise required to evaluate everything coming its way, given the highly specialized skills and knowledge required to operate at the frontiers of mathematics.

Francesco Fournier-Facio, an incoming mathematics professor at Heriot-Watt University in Scotland, described himself as pretty “ambivalent” about the panel, saying that greater engagement with mathematicians “can only make things better.” But he questioned whether this group fully reflects the community whose work and livelihoods are being upended by OpenAI’s quest to rack up mathematical trophies. “It feels like an ivory tower,” he told The Verge.

Machado similarly questioned whether the group’s members fully understand, or can speak to, the concerns of the broader mathematical community when it comes to AI. “They’re amazing mathematicians, but I don’t know if they are the people I want to represent me in more political questions,” he said. For mathematicians in their and similarly elite positions, Machado said, “I think that the reality they are facing is very different from the reality that most mathematicians are facing right now.”

Whether the group can earn mathematicians’ trust will ultimately determine how effective it will be at containing the fallout from OpenAI’s recent parade of missteps in announcing results and, more importantly, soften the blow for whatever the company is planning to announce next. In his blog, Hairer said members would “be very naïve to believe that the AI labs won’t try to spin whatever we say in a way that suits their PR machine, which dwarfs anything we could possibly come up with.”

Nevertheless, Hairer argued it would be hypocritical not to engage now that OpenAI appears to be making an effort, particularly after so many criticized the company’s conduct and poor communications. The group has yet to settle on the advice it intends to provide, he said, but there is a clear problem it is responding to: “It is a fact that AI companies have in recent months been producing some high profile mathematical results and that their publication and dissemination has been falling far short of acceptable mathematical practice, whichever way that is defined.”

“We are currently facing the very specific challenge of advising OpenAI on how to coordinate the release of a large number of significant results in mathematics that they report have been produced by their internal model.”

For now, Hairer said the group is gathering input through conversations with colleagues, a public feedback form, and discussion on Proofs and Prompts, a blog that has emerged as a key forum for mathematicians reckoning with AI’s impact on the field.

But the group’s biggest challenge likely lies ahead. When announcing the advisory group, OpenAI casually dropped the news that its new, unreleased model — the same that resolved the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize problem — has now “resolved more than 100 long-standing open problems across most areas of mathematics.” It has previously said it is closing in on another Millennium Prize problem. On its website, the group said dealing with this logjam is its first priority: “We are currently facing the very specific challenge of advising OpenAI on how to coordinate the release of a large number of significant results in mathematics that they report have been produced by their internal model.”

In part, the new effort at engaging mathematicians is an acknowledgement of the monumental PR disaster its attempt was, in which the company found itself fending off accusations of scooping researchers, failing to credit the human work its models built upon, and even stealing from those using its models. Those controversies led many mathematicians to wonder if the company understood — or even respected — the discipline and community it had barreled into.

After the last few months and with so much having been written about what mathematicians want, Kevin Buzzard, a mathematics professor at Imperial College London, wondered why OpenAI felt like it needed such an elite body to understand what the community wants. “It wasn’t proofs of hard theorems, it was better understanding of our subject,” he said. “It’s not entirely clear to me that you need a committee of brilliant people to hammer the point home.”

fulltext_cn: ﻿“该小组将就新结果的审查和沟通提供建议。”
在将一系列令人惊叹的数学结果变成一场声誉危机后，OpenAI 正在咨询人类数学家，以帮助它找出一条不那么灾难性的前进道路。

周一，该公司宣布成立一个新的独立数学家小组，其任务是就其与数学研究和更广泛的数学社区的互动向该公司和其他人工智能公司提供建议，包括如何呈现和发布新结果。它的突然到来让许多数学家感到惊讶。研究人员告诉 The Verge，该小组是一个很好的第一步，但许多人表示，他们仍然面临一些基本问题，比如它实际上会做什么、会产生多大影响、OpenAI 是否会真正听取它的意见，以及对这样一小群杰出研究人员是否能够代表更广泛的数学界的担忧。
这个由九名成员组成的小组中，有研究人员向 The Verge 描述的该领域的名人，他们来自斯坦福大学、哈佛大学、牛津大学和剑桥大学等机构，其中包括多项菲尔兹奖和麦克阿瑟“天才奖”。它将由新泽西州普林斯顿高等研究院 (IAS) 主办，IAS 是世界上最受尊敬的数学研究中心之一，也是阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦、约翰·冯·诺伊曼和 J·罗伯特·奥本海默等名人的前知识分子故乡。
“另一个基本事实是，我们的首要目标是尽可能代表数学界的利益。”

OpenAI 表示，这个名为数学和人工智能咨询小组 (AGMAI) 的小组将独立运作，可以自由地提供公司未要求的建议、公开评论其对数学的影响，并公开其建议，但它没有提供具体信息。看来该小组将被允许尽早接触 OpenAI 的研究，以完成其任务。 OpenAI 表示，OpenAI 不会向成员支付报酬，并且该组织可以根据需要更改其成员资格。该公司表示：“它的价值取决于其成员能够运用自己的判断并挑战我们的判断。” “该小组将就新兴成果的审查和交流提供建议：他们将帮助 OpenAI 评估其重要性，就如何协调其传播提供建议，并就数学研究的学术和专业标准提供建议。它还将就我们的工具如何支持数学研究和学习提供建议。”

尽管强调独立性，但目前尚不清楚该组织实际上会产生多大的影响力，也不清楚该组织最初为何成立。瑞士苏黎世联邦理工学院研究员西蒙·马查多表示，整件事似乎“笼罩在神秘之中”，他质疑这九名成员是如何选出的。该组织的简体网站称，该组织“是在 OpenAI 与一些成员接触建立外部顾问委员会后组建的”，但在与该公司讨论后，数学家们决定成立一个独立小组，并邀请其他人加入。目前尚不清楚 OpenAI 最初接触了哪些成员，也不清楚其余成员是如何选择的。
在周二发表的一篇博客文章中，顾问小组成员马丁·海尔（Martin Hairer）详细阐述了该小组的起源及其背后的想法，回应了他所说的围绕该小组成立的“大量错误信息”。他写道：“显然，人工智能已经对数学研究产生了深远的影响，并提出了许多关于思想的正确归属、优先级、人类对思想的理解等问题。”他补充说，社区中“采取强硬的‘鸵鸟’方式，简单地忽略人工智能实验室并原则上拒绝与他们交谈”是没有意义的。
海勒承认该组织是为了回应 OpenAI 的建议而成立，但他强调，该公司并未联系过该组织的所有成员，并且该组织“真正独立于 OpenAI 和任何其他所谓的‘前沿’人工智能实验室。”他表示，除了“明显的保密要求”之外，成员还没有签署任何限制他们可以公开发表言论的限制性协议，并补充说他们没有获得任何经济补偿，并且依赖 IAS 提供技术支持。
“另一个基本事实是，我们的首要目标是尽可能代表数学界的利益，”伦敦帝国理工学院和洛桑瑞士联邦理工学院 (EPFL) 的数学教授海勒写道。他指出，该组织很难成为社区的代表性样本，但他表示“绝对确定我们九个人都非常认真地对待这一问题，并真诚地行事。”
不管成员是如何选择的，该小组目前由学术数学家组成的精英骨干队伍组成。鉴于在数学前沿运作所需的高度专业化的技能和知识，规模较小引发了进一步的问题：该小组是否拥有评估即将发生的一切所需的广泛专业知识。
苏格兰赫瑞瓦特大学即将上任的数学教授弗朗西斯科·福尼耶-法西奥 (Francesco Fournier-Facio) 表示，自己对这个小组的态度相当“矛盾”，他表示，与数学家的更多接触“只会让事情变得更好”。但他质疑这个群体是否充分反映了 OpenAI 对数学奖杯的追求正在颠覆其工作和生计的社区。 “感觉就像一座象牙塔，”他告诉 The Verge。
马查多同样质疑该小组的成员是否完全理解或能够表达更广泛的数学界对人工智能的担忧。 “他们是令人惊叹的数学家，但我不知道他们是否是我想在更多政治问题上代表我的人，”他说。马查多说，对于处于同样精英地位的数学家来说，“我认为他们面临的现实与大多数数学家现在面临的现实非常不同。”
该组织能否赢得数学家的信任，最终将决定它能否有效地遏制 OpenAI 最近在宣布结果方面的一系列失误所带来的影响，更重要的是，它能否有效地减轻该公司接下来计划宣布的任何消息所带来的打击。海勒在他的博客中表示，成员们“如果相信人工智能实验室不会试图以适合他们公关机器的方式来歪曲我们所说的一切，那就太天真了，这让我们可能想出的任何东西都相形见绌。”
尽管如此，海勒认为，既然 OpenAI 似乎正在做出努力，那么不参与是虚伪的，尤其是在许多人批评该公司的行为和沟通不畅之后。他说，该组织尚未就其打算提供的建议达成一致，但它正在回应一个明显的问题：“事实上，人工智能公司近几个月来已经产生了一些引人注目的数学结果，但无论以哪种方式定义，它们的出版和传播都远远低于可接受的数学实践。”
“我们目前面临着一个非常具体的挑战，即向 OpenAI 提供建议，说明如何协调发布大量重要的数学成果，他们报告说这些成果是由其内部模型产生的。”
海勒表示，目前该小组正在通过与同事的对话、公众反馈表以及“证明和提示”上的讨论来收集意见，“证明和提示”博客已成为数学家考虑人工智能对该领域影响的重要论坛。

但该集团最大的挑战可能还在前方。在宣布成立顾问小组时，OpenAI 不经意地透露，其未发布的新模型（解决了纳维-斯托克斯千年奖问题的模型）现在已经“解决了大多数数学领域的 100 多个长期悬而未决的问题”。该公司此前曾表示，即将解决另一个千年奖问题。该组织在其网站上表示，解决这一僵局是其首要任务：“我们目前面临着一项非常具体的挑战，即如何协调 OpenAI 报告其内部模型产生的大量重要数学结果的发布，为 OpenAI 提供建议。”
在某种程度上，吸引数学家参与的新努力是对其尝试所造成的巨大公关灾难的承认，在这场灾难中，该公司发现自己面临着挖取研究人员、未能信任其模型所建立的人类工作成果、甚至从使用其模型的人那里窃取的指控。这些争议让许多数学家怀疑该公司是否理解——甚至尊重——它所融入的学科和社区。
在过去的几个月里，关于数学家想要什么的文章已经写了很多，伦敦帝国理工学院的数学教授 Kevin Buzzard 想知道为什么 OpenAI 觉得它需要这样一个精英团体来了解社区的需求。 “这不是证明硬定理，而是更好地理解我们的主题，”他说。 “我并不完全清楚你是否需要一个由才华横溢的人组成的委员会来强调这一点。”

On November 4, TechCrunch’s Founder Summit will bring a vital one-day crash course on startup building to Boston’s SoWa Power Station. Founders shouldn’t have to learn the hardest lessons the hardest way, and this event is designed to make the challenges of starting a company easier and the highs that much greater.

Instead of months of trial and error, you get direct access to the investors and founders who’ve already made the calls you’re now facing. We’re talking everything from fundraising and hiring to AI strategy, and topping your category.

Don’t take our word for it. Explore the full agenda of speakers and sessions we have planned for Founder Summit below, and lock in your spot at the event. All tickets are available for the lowest prices you’ll see, so now’s the best time to act.
Without further ado, here’s the official agenda. Get to know each session and speaker on the event agenda page.

Fundraising has never been easy, but the playbook keeps changing. Brian Devaney, partner at Underscore, will break down what investors are looking for now, how founders can stand out in a crowded market, and where founders often lose leverage without realizing it. Expect a candid look at today’s fundraising environment, from first checks to term sheets, and the mistakes that can make or break a round.

The title may stay the same, but the job changes with each stage of a company’s growth. HubSpot co-founder and Sequoia partner Brian Halligan will share the lessons he’s learned from building and advising startups through rapid growth, tough decisions, and constant reinvention.
This session explores how founders can evolve as CEOs, avoid common leadership pitfalls, and build companies that can thrive well beyond the early days.

Adding AI features is one thing. Building an AI-native company is something else entirely. Lior Div, co-founder and CEO of 7AI, will explore what changes when AI becomes the foundation of a startup rather than a product enhancement. From team structure and product development to operations and go-to-market strategy, this session examines what founders should rethink when building in the AI era.

Raising capital is often framed as a milestone, but choosing the right investors can shape a company’s future long after the money arrives. After raising an $11 million round for Cogent Security, co-founder and CEO Vineet Edupuganti learned firsthand what separates helpful partners from costly distractions. This session explores how founders should evaluate investors, navigate trade-offs, and think beyond valuation when building their cap table.

Innovation is needed to solve the world’s biggest challenges, but only certain companies can realistically become category-defining winners at industrial scale. In this session, TDK Ventures investment director Tina Tosukhowong unpacks the firm’s “King of the Hill” framework: the disciplined process that the best investors use to evaluate companies based on economics, scalability, and commercial timing.

Through real-world examples, including Tina’s exploration of fission and fusion, attendees will learn actionable frameworks for evaluating startup readiness, mapping competitive landscapes, and identifying when timing, talent, and technology align.

Early hiring decisions can define a startup’s culture, speed, and ability to execute. Melissa Taunton, partner at NEA, will share lessons from working with founders as they build teams through periods of rapid growth and uncertainty.

From identifying the right early hires to avoiding common recruiting mistakes, this session explores how founders can build organizations that are resilient, adaptable, and prepared for what comes next.

Silicon Valley gets the headlines, but Chase Garbarino has been quietly building category-defining companies from Boston for over a decade. As co-founder and CEO of HqO, he has raised $200 million from investors and scaled to 30+ countries without ever needing to change geographies.
He’ll break down the real advantages and disadvantages of building where the startup playbook wasn’t written, and what every founder outside a major hub should know.

Every founder wants product-market fit, but knowing when you’ve actually found it is far more complicated. Kent Bennett, partner at Bessemer Venture Partners, will unpack how founders can validate demand, build an MVP that answers the right questions, and avoid scaling before the fundamentals are in place.
This session explores the signals that matter, the metrics that mislead, and the decisions that separate enduring companies from expensive experiments.

The programming is a huge part of TechCrunch Founder Summit’s value, but it’s not the whole deal. You’ll also get the chance to mix and mingle with founders working through the same fundraising decisions and the same hiring calls as you, and then network with those who have already lived through those experiences. Or better yet … those who have funded those who have gone through the startup wringer.

A day filled with discussions turns into months of action at TechCrunch Founder Summit, and we’re eager for you to join us and the rest of the Boston startup community on November 4. Register now to secure your ticket savings and join the ultimate founder’s bootcamp.

cards.summary: 【Anthropic】TL;DR Anthropic’s new Claude Opus 5.5 promises improved performance, accuracy, communication, and stronger safety safeguards. The model generates responses over 30% faster and costs roughly 40% less t…

When it comes to AI, performance, accuracy, and pricing are the biggest considerations for power users. With Claude Opus 5, Anthropic achieved impressive results on the performance and accuracy fronts, but access to the model came at a premium. With the company’s latest model released today, that’s less of a concern.
Anthropic announced Claude Opus 5.5 today, and the new model promises not only better performance and accuracy, but also a roughly 40% reduction in running costs compared to Opus 5.
According to the company, the new model is the strongest-performing model it has tested to date. Of course, with that come concerns, which Anthropic says it is tackling with new safeguards.
For starters, the new model communicates better. Anthropic says this was a concern for users with Opus 5.

According to early testers, Opus 5.5 communicates more naturally, with its writing being clearer and easier to follow. Messages are much easier to parse at a glance, which, according to testers, is helpful during long working sessions. “Verbose, hard-to-follow output has been my biggest frustration with frontier models, and Claude Opus 5.5 fixes it. It writes like a good colleague, and follows our writing rules,” wrote a Ramp software engineer, while a principal engineer at the Chicago Trading Company wrote, “Its writing is easy to follow and more coherent than Opus 5’s.”

When it comes to performance, Opus 5.5 leads models like Fable 5.1, Opus 5, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-5.6 Sol in benchmarks like agentic coding, knowledge work, multidisciplinary reasoning, computer use, and visual chart recognition. In benchmarks like business workflows and agentic scientific research, the new model ranked second, only behind GPT-6 Astra, all while generating output 30% faster than Opus 5.

Of course, benchmarks only tell part of the story, so Anthropic brought real-world receipts. According to the company, an early tester was able to audit and fix a 200,000-line codebase in under three hours. Opus 5 took over 20 hours and 2.5x as many tokens to complete the same task. Similarly, in a test that tasked the AI model with translating software from C into Rust, Opus 5.5 took 9.5 hours. Fable 5.1 took 12 hours to complete the same task.

Anthropic also shared examples of similar efficiency and intelligence gains from early testers at GitHub, Clio, Lovable, Quantum, Spotify, and more. The tester at GitHub found that the model solved more terminal tasks than Opus 5 in less than half the steps, while the tester at Spotify hyped the model for being able to complete tasks for cheaper and faster than previous models.

Elsewhere, Anthropic touted the model’s native classifier, which essentially screens every action before it runs. The model also reportedly has stronger defenses than predecessors. It reportedly matches or beats Opus 5 in mitigating prompt injection attacks in every setting, including coding, tool use, computer use, and web browsing. “On a benchmark run by the AI security firm Gray Swan, Opus 5.5 ties Fable 5.1 for the lowest prompt injection success rate of any model tested,” the company added.

Perhaps the biggest attraction here is that Anthropic isn’t charging you more for all the improvements. API pricing has dropped from $5 on Opus 5 to $4 on Opus 5.5 per million input tokens. Similarly, pricing has dropped from $25 to $20 per million output tokens. Cache reads cost $0.20 per million tokens, down from $0.50, while cache writes cost $5 per million tokens, down from $6.25. According to the company, overall, with improvements in token efficiency, running Opus 5.5 will cost roughly 40% less than Opus 5 on typical workloads.

More importantly, you don’t really need to be a developer or use APIs to access Claude Opus 5.5. It is available to regular users too, with five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. Find more information, including detailed early tester testimonials, on Anthropic’s blog post, linked up top.

在人工智能方面，性能、准确性和定价是高级用户最大的考虑因素。借助Claude Opus 5 ， Anthropic在性能和准确性方面取得了令人印象深刻的成果，但获得该模型的机会非常宝贵。随着该公司今天发布的最新车型，这不是一个令人担忧的问题。
Anthropic今天发布了Claude Opus 5.5 ，新型号不仅保证了更好的性能和准确性，而且与Opus 5相比，运行成本降低了约40 ％。
据该公司称，新车型是迄今为止测试过的性能最强的车型。当然，随之而来的是人们的担忧， Anthropic表示它正在通过新的保障措施来应对这些担忧。
对于初学者来说，新模型可以更好地沟通。Anthropic表示，这是Opus 5用户关注的问题。

根据早期测试人员的说法， Opus 5.5的沟通更自然，其文字更清晰，更容易理解。消息更容易一目了然，根据测试人员的说法，这在长时间的工作会话中很有帮助。“冗长、难以遵循的输出是我对前沿模型最大的挫败感， Claude Opus 5.5修复了它。它像一个好同事一样写作，并遵循我们的写作规则， ”一位Ramp软件工程师写道，而芝加哥贸易公司的一位首席工程师写道，“它的写作很容易理解，比Opus 5的作品更连贯。”
在性能方面， Opus 5.5在代理编码、知识工作、多学科推理、计算机使用和视觉图表识别等基准方面领先于Fable 5.1、Opus 5、GPT-6 Astra和GPT-5.6 Sol等模型。在业务工作流程和代理科学研究等基准中，新模型排名第二，仅次于GPT-6 Astra ，同时产生的产出比Opus 5快30%。
当然，基准测试只能说明部分故事，因此Anthropic带来了真实世界的收据。据该公司称，早期的测试人员能够在三小时内审核并修复20万行代码库。Opus 5花了20多个小时和2.5倍的代币来完成相同的任务。同样，在让人工智能模型将软件从C翻译成Rust的测试中， Opus 5.5花了9.5个小时。寓言5.1花了12个小时才完成同样的任务。
Anthropic还分享了GitHub、Clio、Lovable、Quantum、Spotify等早期测试人员的类似效率和智能提升的例子。GitHub的测试人员发现，该模型在不到一半的步骤中解决了比Opus 5更多的终端任务，而Spotify的测试人员大肆宣传该模型能够以比以前的模型更便宜、更快的速度完成任务。

在其他地方， Anthropic吹捧了模型的原生分类器，它本质上是在运行之前筛选每个动作。据报道，该型号还具有比前辈更强的防御能力。据报道，它在减轻各种环境中的提示注入攻击方面与Opus 5相匹配或优于Opus 5 ，包括编码、工具使用、计算机使用和网页浏览。该公司补充说： “在人工智能安全公司Gray Swan运行的基准测试中， Opus 5.5与Fable 5.1并列，获得了所有测试模型中最低的即时注入成功率。”

也许这里最大的吸引力在于， Anthropic并没有为所有改进向您收取更多费用。API定价已从Opus 5的5美元降至Opus 5.5每百万个输入代币的4美元。同样，每百万个输出代币的定价从25美元降至2000美元。缓存读取成本为每百万令牌0.20美元，低于0.50美元，而缓存写入成本为每百万令牌5美元，低于6.25美元。根据该公司的说法，总体而言，随着代币效率的提高，在典型工作负载上运行Opus 5.5的成本将比Opus 5低约40 ％。
更重要的是，您无需成为开发人员或使用API访问Claude Opus 5.5。它也适用于普通用户，基于Pro、Max、Team和座位的企业版套餐有五小时的使用限制。在顶部链接的Anthropic博客文章中查找更多信息，包括详细的早期测试人员推荐。
